column1: # The timeline divergence corpus: the series where ical-rs deliberately answers
# something neither oracle does, recurring-ical-events 3.9.0 nor ical.js 2.2.1
# calendar, the UID, the occurrences ical-rs yields (as in agreement.tsv), and
# why that is the answer, with what each oracle answers instead.
# Hand-curated, unlike agreement.tsv and split.tsv beside it: each line was
# read against the calendar and settled on 2026-10-29. No series has both
# oracles agreeing against ical-rs. Both oracles also refuse twelve libical
# calendars outright, from which ical-rs yields no series either, so they have
# no line: caltime, crash, get_char_test, issue250, issue251, issue252,
# issue253, issue339, malloc, stresstest, test_2446 and zday, all malformed.

column4: One UID shared by a VEVENT and a VTODO is one series, the highest SEQUENCE (here the last listed of equals) being it, and its end before its start is swapped: recurring-ical-events yields one occurrence per component; ical.js yields one per component too and keeps each end before its start (20231218T224500Z/20231218T223000Z).

DTSTART is a date and DTEND a date-time (RFC 5545 3.8.2.2 wants the same type): the same instants, the start kept a date. recurring-ical-events promotes the start to a date-time; ical.js keeps the start a date but cuts the end to a date too (20000102), adding the span to the date.

DTSTART a date with an hours-only DURATION: the same instants, the start kept a date. recurring-ical-events promotes the start to a date-time; ical.js keeps the start a date and drops the hours, ending at the start (20000101).

DTSTART a date, DTEND a UTC date-time: the same instants, the start kept a date and read floating. recurring-ical-events promotes both to UTC; ical.js keeps the start a date but cuts the end to a date (20000103).

DTSTART a date, DUE a date-time: the same instants, the start kept a date. recurring-ical-events promotes the start to a date-time; ical.js keeps the start a date but cuts the end to a date (20000102).

DTSTART a date with an hours-only DURATION: the same instants, the start kept a date. recurring-ical-events promotes the start to a date-time; ical.js keeps the start a date and drops the hours, ending at the start (20000101).

DTSTART a date, DUE a UTC date-time: the same instants, the start kept a date and read floating. recurring-ical-events promotes both to UTC; ical.js keeps the start a date but cuts the end to a date (20000103).
